explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't sugarcoat it. He calls them “…seven nations larger and stronger than you…” So Israel is the underdog in this picture, and I think Moses is building toward something with that. Keep this one in your pocket, friend.

Moses actually says it the other way around. He calls the seven nations “…larger and stronger than you…” That would make for an easy walk into the land, and Moses doesn't describe it that way. Israel is facing bigger neighbors.

explanations.answer: About the same size as Israel
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't call it an even match. He says the seven nations are “…larger and stronger than you…” That's a tougher spot than a fair fight. Hold on to that detail, because it matters later in the sermon.
Moses says the opposite. His words are “Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.” No handshakes and no paperwork. It's one of the plainest lines in the whole passage.
That's right. Moses says, “Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.” He doesn't leave any room for a deal. The text is plain on this one.

That's it. Moses says, “Do not intermarry with them.” He spells it out, too: Israel isn't to give their daughters to the nations' sons or take the nations' daughters for their own sons. It's a clear line, right after the one about treaties.
Moses doesn't say a word about trade in this passage. What he says is, “Do not intermarry with them.” He's talking about daughters and sons, not goods. Easy one to slide past if you're reading fast.

Travel doesn't come up here. Moses says, “Do not intermarry with them,” and he goes on to say not to give daughters to their sons or take their daughters for Israel's sons. The word he uses is a family word, not a road word.

explanations.answer: They would turn Israel's sons away to serve other gods
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Moses gives. He says, “…they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods.” It's about who Israel's sons would end up following. Moses puts it right there in verse 4.

explanations.answer: They would claim a share of the land Israel was given
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't give a land reason here. He says, “…they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods.” The worry he names is about following other gods. Nobody is splitting up property in this verse.

explanations.answer: They would bring their armies right into Israel's camp
explanations.explanation: No armies show up in this verse. Moses says the danger is that “…they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods.” The concern is where Israel's sons would end up following. That's the reason he gives, and he doesn't give another.
Right on target. Moses says, “…burn their idols in the fire.” The altars, pillars and poles each get their own action, and the idols get the fire. Verse 5 reads like a full work order.

explanations.answer: Bury them deep in the ground
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't mention a shovel. He says to “…burn their idols in the fire.” Fire is the word he uses for the idols. Burying isn't in his list.
There's no river in this verse. Moses says to “…burn their idols in the fire.” The tearing down and smashing are for the altars and pillars, and the fire is for the idols.

That's the word Moses uses. He says the LORD has chosen Israel “…to be a people for His prized possession out of all peoples on the face of the earth.” Out of every people on earth, He picked them. That's the heart of verse 6.

Moses doesn't call them hired workers. He says the LORD has chosen Israel “…to be a people for His prized possession out of all peoples on the face of the earth.” A prized possession is not a paycheck kind of word. It's a treasured kind of word.

Moses never calls them border guards. He says the LORD chose them “…to be a people for His prized possession out of all peoples on the face of the earth.” He starts that sentence with “For you are a people holy to the LORD your God.” It's about who they are to Him.

Moses says the reverse. He says the LORD did not choose them because they were more numerous, “…for you were the fewest of all peoples.” The headcount wasn't the reason. Israel was the smallest group in the room.

That's right. Moses says the LORD did not choose them because they were more numerous, “…for you were the fewest of all peoples.” Numbers didn't win Israel the spot. Hold onto that, because Moses tells them the real reason next.

Yes, loved. Moses says, “…the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers…” It wasn't size or strength that got them picked. I know a little about being chosen when nobody was counting. A quarter, a closing bakery bin, and Mother Miller smiling at me.
Moses never says the LORD needed them. He says, “…the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers…” The reason is love and a promise. Needing doesn't appear in the verse.

Moses doesn't say trusted here. He says, “…the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers…” The reason he gives is love, and a promise that was already made. That's the word to remember.

That's right. Moses says, “…the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations…” and he says it's for those who love Him and keep His commandments. A thousand generations is a long, long time. That's a lot of keeping.

Moses really does say this. He calls the LORD “…the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations…” and says it's for those who love Him and keep His commandments. It's right there in verse 9. The statement on the card is exactly what the text says.

explanations.answer: Keep the commandments he is giving them
explanations.explanation: That's the conclusion Moses draws. He says, “So keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances that I am giving you to follow this day.” Everything he's said about the LORD leads to that one word: keep. Verse 11 is the landing spot.

explanations.answer: Send spies ahead into the land first
explanations.explanation: Spies aren't mentioned in this passage. Moses says, “So keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances that I am giving you to follow this day.” That's the instruction right after what he says about the LORD. No scouting party in sight.

explanations.answer: Wait by the river for another sign
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't tell them to wait for a sign. He says, “So keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances that I am giving you to follow this day.” The instruction is about what they do with what he's already given them. I'd say that's plenty to be going on with.

explanations.answer: Their children and their land and their flocks
explanations.explanation: Yes. Moses says the LORD “…will bless the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land…” and he adds the young of their herds and the lambs of their flocks. Children, land and flocks, all covered in verse 13. He says it's in the land the LORD swore to their fathers to give them.

explanations.answer: Their swords and their shields and their walls
explanations.explanation: No weapons or walls are in this list. Moses talks about the fruit of the womb, the produce of the land, grain, new wine and oil, and the young of the herds and lambs of the flocks. It's a list about family and harvest. Nobody's getting a blessed shield.

explanations.answer: Their tents and their tools and their wagons
explanations.explanation: Tents, tools and wagons aren't on Moses' list. He says the LORD will bless the fruit of their womb and the produce of their land, including grain, new wine and oil. He also names the young of their herds and the lambs of their flocks. That's the whole list in verse 13.
That's right. Moses says, “And the LORD will remove from you all sickness.” He adds that Israel won't be given the terrible diseases they knew in Egypt. All means all in that sentence.
Moses really does say this. His words are, “And the LORD will remove from you all sickness.” It's a big promise and he says it plainly. The card's sentence matches verse 15.
That's the word. Moses says, “Do not worship their gods, for that will be a snare to you.” A snare is a trap, and it catches the one who walks into it. He says the trap would be for Israel.
Moses doesn't call it a burden on the land. He says, “Do not worship their gods, for that will be a snare to you.” The word he picks is snare. It's about what would catch Israel.
Shame before the nations isn't in this verse. Moses says, “Do not worship their gods, for that will be a snare to you.” The word to hold onto is snare. That's what he says it would be.

That's the word. Moses says, “Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt.” He tells them not to be afraid and to look back instead. I've been known to search for my hat while wearing it, so I respect anyone who sets up a reminder.

Moses doesn't say announce. He says, “Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt.” Before anything gets said out loud, it has to be kept in mind. Remember is the word in verse 18.
Repeat isn't the word Moses uses. He says, “Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt.” The instruction is about remembering. That's what he asks of Israel.

Yes, the hornet. Moses says, “Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet against them until even the survivors hiding from you have perished.” Even the ones hiding don't get away. The text gives only that one word for it.
Moses doesn't say locust. He says the LORD “…will send the hornet against them…” The hornet is the creature named in verse 20. It reaches even the survivors who are hiding.

No serpent in this verse. Moses says the LORD “…will send the hornet against them…” and he says it keeps going until even the survivors hiding from Israel have perished. The hornet is the answer here.
Moses says the opposite. He says, “The LORD your God will drive out these nations before you little by little.” It's a slow process by design. All at once isn't what the verse says.

That's right. Moses says, “The LORD your God will drive out these nations before you little by little.” He also says Israel will not be enabled to eliminate them all at once. A little at a time is how verse 22 puts it.

explanations.answer: The wild animals would multiply around Israel
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Moses gives. He says Israel will not be enabled to eliminate them all at once, “…or the wild animals would multiply around you.” So the pace is little by little. The text gives that one reason.

explanations.answer: Israel's army would grow too tired to fight
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say anything about a tired army. He says it's little by little “…or the wild animals would multiply around you.” That's the reason in verse 22. Fatigue isn't in the verse.

explanations.answer: The land would be left without any farmers
explanations.explanation: Farmers aren't part of this verse. Moses says Israel will not be enabled to eliminate them all at once, “…or the wild animals would multiply around you.” That's his stated reason. Nothing about the land going unfarmed.

Moses says the opposite. He says the LORD “…will hand their kings over to you…” and then, “No one will be able to stand against you…” He doesn't carve out a few exceptions. That's the whole promise in verse 24.
That's right. Moses says, “No one will be able to stand against you…” He doesn't leave a few nations standing. It comes right after he says the LORD will hand their kings over to Israel.

explanations.answer: It is detestable to the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Moses gives. He says not to covet the silver and gold on the images “…or you will be ensnared by it; for it is detestable to the LORD your God.” So Israel is to burn the images and leave the metal alone. That's the stated reason in verse 25.

Priests aren't mentioned in this verse. Moses says not to covet the silver and gold on the images “…or you will be ensnared by it; for it is detestable to the LORD your God.” That's the reason he gives. Nothing about who owns it.

explanations.answer: It is owed to the kings
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say anything about it being owed to kings. He says the silver and gold would ensnare Israel, “…for it is detestable to the LORD your God.” That's the reason in verse 25. Keep your eyes on that phrase.

That's the word. Moses says, “And you must not bring any detestable thing into your house, or you, like it, will be set apart for destruction.” It's a heavy line, and he says it plainly. He means it as a warning to keep that thing out of the house.

Moses doesn't say service. He says anyone who brings in a detestable thing “…like it, will be set apart for destruction.” It's a heavy word, and it's the one in verse 26. Service doesn't appear in that verse.

Cleansing isn't the word Moses uses. He says anyone who brings a detestable thing into the house “…like it, will be set apart for destruction.” It's a serious line, and the text states it plainly. That's the word to remember.
